FISHING LICENCE · AUSTRALIA

Western Australia fishing licence

Western Australia has no general fishing licence. Line fishing from the shore, a jetty or a boat without a motor needs no licence. You need a licence for six activities: fishing from a powered boat ($40 a year), and south-west freshwater angling, rock lobster, abalone, marron and net fishing ($50 a year each). The department lists one fee for each licence. There is no separate visitor price.

Visitor licence from$40 AUD12 months
Buy on the official site ↗Checked against official sources on 27 Nov 2026.

1Who needs a fishing licence in Western Australia?

You need a licence

  • Anyone who fishes from a powered boat: line fishing, squid jigging, crabbing, spearfishing, catching octopus and dip netting for prawns. Catch and release also needs the licence.
  • Anyone who uses a powered boat to carry their catch or fishing gear from a land-based spot, including an island or a sandbar.
  • Anglers aged 16 and older who fish freshwater south of Greenough (29°S) and above the tidal influence, including lakes, dams, rivers and their tributaries.
  • Anyone who fishes for rock lobster, abalone or marron, or who uses a haul, set or throw net.

You do not need one

  • Line fishing from the shore, a jetty or a boat without a motor needs no licence.
  • You need no boat licence on a licensed fishing tour or fishing charter boat.
  • You need no boat licence when another person on board holds one. The total catch of everyone on board must stay within the bag limit of the licensed fishers. This rule applies to the boat licence only.
  • You need no boat licence when the only fishing on the boat is an activity that you already hold a licence for, such as rock lobster, abalone or south-west freshwater angling.
  • Anglers under 16 do not need the south-west freshwater angling licence.
  • Crab drop netting, crab scoop netting and prawn netting need no net fishing licence, unless you use a throw net.
  • An Aboriginal person who fishes in accordance with customary law and tradition, for personal, family or non-commercial community needs, does not need a recreational fishing licence.

3Where can you buy the licence?

Apply or renew online through the Department of Transport's DoTDirect website. You can also post the application form with payment to the department, or pay in person at a department office. Existing licence holders get a renewal form by post.

Buy on the official site ↗

4Rules to know before you fish

  • You are not entitled to fish until you receive a receipt for your licence from the department.
  • A licence is valid for 12 months from the date of payment. The plastic licence card arrives within 30 days.
  • Carry your licence at all times when you fish. Produce it when a Fisheries and Marine Officer asks.
  • Apply for more than one licence type in a single transaction and the department gives a 10% discount.
  • To take a boat limit on a powered boat, two or more boat licence holders must be on board. This includes crabbing.
  • South-west freshwater angling: the daily mixed bag limit is 4 rainbow trout, brown trout and freshwater cobbler combined for each licensed angler. The minimum size for trout is 300 mm.
  • Marron: the open season is from 12 noon on 8 January to 12 noon on 5 February. Fishing for marron and transporting marron are prohibited at all other times.
  • Rock lobster pots and nets must show your gear identification number on every float.
  • All drinking water supply dams managed by Water Corporation are closed to fishing.

Questions before your trip

Saltwater fishing

Shore, beach and jetty line fishing in the sea needs no licence. From a powered boat you need the $40 boat licence. Rock lobster, abalone and net fishing each need their own licence.

Fishing with a guide or charter

Clients on a licensed fishing tour or charter boat do not need the boat licence. Fishers on a fishing tour do not need a rock lobster licence to possess rock lobster.

What to confirm before the trip

Fees and rules are from the department's licence page and its 2026 guides. Abalone seasons, zones and bag limits change each year; read the current guide before you fish.

Do you need a fishing licence in Western Australia?

Not for line fishing from the shore, a jetty or a boat without a motor. You need a licence for six activities: fishing from a powered boat, south-west freshwater angling, rock lobster, abalone, marron and net fishing.

How much is a fishing licence in WA?

The Recreational Fishing from Boat Licence costs $40 for 12 months. The south-west freshwater angling, rock lobster, abalone, marron and net fishing licences cost $50 each for 12 months. A single application for more than one licence type gets a 10% discount.

Do I need a licence to fish from the shore or a jetty in WA?

No. Shore, beach and jetty line fishing in the sea needs no licence. You need a licence on the shore only for a licensed activity: rock lobster, abalone, marron, net fishing, or freshwater angling south of Greenough.

Do pensioners and seniors pay for a fishing licence in WA?

They pay half the fee. The concession applies to holders of a Seniors Card issued by the Department of Communities and to people who receive an age, disability support or widow's pension, or a listed veterans' pension. Their spouse or de facto partner also pays half.

Do children need a fishing licence in WA?

Anglers under 16 do not need the south-west freshwater angling licence. For the other licences, a person under 16 pays half the fee. On a powered boat, a child can fish without a licence when a licence holder on board shares their bag limit.

Do tourists need a fishing licence in Western Australia?

Yes, for the six licensed activities. The department lists one fee for each licence, with no separate visitor price. A visitor who only fishes with a line from the shore or a jetty needs no licence, and clients on a licensed fishing charter need no boat licence.

Does everyone on the boat need a licence?

No. Unlicensed people can fish when one or more people on board hold the boat licence. The total catch of everyone on board must stay within the bag limit of the licence holders. To take a boat limit, two or more licence holders must be on board.

Do I need a licence for crabbing in WA?

From a powered boat, yes: crabbing needs the $40 boat licence. Crab drop netting and scoop netting do not need the net fishing licence.

How long does a WA fishing licence last?

12 months from the date of payment. The department sends the plastic licence card within 30 days. You can fish from the time you receive the receipt for your licence.
